criteria.name: Generalization
reasons: The core approach models the environment (rails, walls, envelope), not object classes, which fits spec 8.4.

The pre-registered placement study (plans committed at 20:48:14, results written 21:00 and 21:07) improves 544 -> 723 frames with 0 paired controls. It is identical per case across the 27.09 revisions and gives 722 with gauge.reference 0, so this gain does not rest on the sensor frame. It still reuses seen shapes on seen backgrounds.

The opinion's held-out ride gain is small (43 -> 37 events, 35 -> 34 episodes). It is trained on 205 negative rows from the same six recordings and ride, plus synthetic positives. Fold thresholds range from 0.0061 to 0.0327, and the 2x margin was chosen on the cross-fit measurement itself.

Rules sized to single set O objects, from my own probes: floating_free_max_dy 1.2 sits in a window between 1.1 (edge cube #4 falls back to 9 frames from 18.3 m) and 1.35 (outside cube #5 becomes a false STOP in 3 frames). The value costs nothing on the five empty recordings (identical alarm frames at 0.95).

Other rules are sized to single cases. The column trim targets one 26.09 clear-run STOP. The body exemption was introduced for #6. The union's edge gains come from the organizers' sensor-axis placement and the rig's yaw sign (median -0.2 to -0.3 deg; -1.16 deg on doubleT_obstacle).

claims_found_wrong_or_overstated: The cycle record attributes the edge cube gain (5.2 -> 35.0 m) 'entirely' to the envelope reference. With gauge.reference 3 but floating_free_max_dy 0.95 or 1.1, #4 STOPs in only 9 frames from 18.3 m. The 35 m also needs the 1.2 value, which sits in an undisclosed window between #4 (above 1.1) and the outside cube #5 (false STOP at 1.35).

README calls the placement improvement a 'held-out gain'. The cycle record itself says it only measures sensitivity to new combinations of seen shapes and seen backgrounds, and floating_free_max_dy was tuned on the same cube shape.

On doubleT_obstacle the person gain is described as 'the organizers' sensor-axis frame'. At 55 m the rail axis there is about 1.1 m off the sensor axis (-1.16 deg), so the reference is the rail envelope shifted by the 0.2 m clamp: a yaw-sign-dependent one-sided widening.

Far evidence is said to hold a track advisory 'only while the gauge vote needs the far hits'. But _clean_gauge counts the far hits in the denominator, so far hits can make a vote fail that the clean hits alone would pass: a delayed STOP (set F 1 m box -2 frames at 83-85 m). This is only partly acknowledged in Limits.
The headline and deck lead with the in-sample ride figure 32 / 2.5 per km (labelled). The opinion's measured held-out effect on STOP episodes is only 35 -> 34, and on alarm frames 176 -> 170.
PRESENTATION.md's 27.09 status says tests/test_overview_video.py still reads _ride_p3d; this cycle already changed it to pick the baseline by its 'created' stamp (stale).
The P3d placement baseline (544 of 2458) was run on a 26.09 working tree whose config.py, detector.py and health.py hashes differ from e7aee6e (minor provenance gap).
safety_concerns: The learned track opinion can withhold a real STOP for up to 10 frames (~1 s, ~20 m at 72 km/h) beyond 25 m, or beyond 40 m for bodies at least 1 m tall. Perturbing only the real person's lateral spread (0.3) and range (120 m) drops the score to 0.011, below the 0.015 threshold. The held-out benefit bought with this risk is only 6 ride events, 1 episode and 6 alarm frames.

The union reference is an asymmetric, rig-yaw-dependent widening of up to 0.2 m within 60 m on straight track. Protection differs left vs right, it steps off at 60 m, and its set O gains rely on the organizers' sensor-axis placement frame (question Q1 to the organizers is still open).
column_width_trim can demote a tall (>2.2 m) irregular object with sparse lateral tails (box width 1.0-1.35 m) to advisory. It was sized to one 26.09 clear-run false alarm.
Far evidence can delay the STOP of a dense object whose track began as far scan lines (set F 1 m box -2 frames at 83-85 m); the track is advisory meanwhile.

Known blind spots remain: an edge object 0.1 m inside the envelope is never STOP at 50-100 m (0 of 126), set F's 0.5 m bed box is detected in 1 of 6 approaches, and 0.3 m cubes STOP only from 43-56 m.
The held-out false-alarm rate is still 2.8 per km (37 events in a 20-minute ride).
